# dlarrf

> Finds a new relatively robust representation for a tridiagonal cluster.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import dlarrf from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/dlarrf';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
dlarrf(
    N,
    d, strideD,
    l, strideL,
    ld, strideLD,
    clstrt, clend,
    w, strideW,
    wgap, strideWGAP,
    werr, strideWERR,
    spdiam, clgapl, clgapr, pivmin,
    sigma,
    dplus, strideDPLUS,
    lplus, strideLPLUS,
    work
) → info: integer
```

Finds a new relatively robust representation (RRR) for a tridiagonal cluster.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Order of the tridiagonal matrix |
| `d` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | Diagonal of the parent representation |
| ↳ `strideD` | `integer` | Stride length for `d` |
| `l` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N - 1</sub> | Subdiagonal of the unit bidiagonal factor |
| ↳ `strideL` | `integer` | Stride length for `l` |
| `ld` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N - 1</sub> | Elementwise product L\*D |
| ↳ `strideLD` | `integer` | Stride length for `ld` |
| `clstrt` | `integer` | First index of the cluster (1-based) |
| `clend` | `integer` | Last index of the cluster (1-based) |
| `w` | `Float64Array` | Approximate eigenvalues of the parent |
| ↳ `strideW` | `integer` | Stride length for `w` |
| `wgap` | `Float64Array` | **in/out** · Approximate gaps between eigenvalues |
| ↳ `strideWGAP` | `integer` | Stride length for `wgap` |
| `werr` | `Float64Array` | Errors in the approximate eigenvalues |
| ↳ `strideWERR` | `integer` | Stride length for `werr` |
| `spdiam` | `number` | Estimate of the spectral diameter |
| `clgapl` | `number` | Left gap of the cluster |
| `clgapr` | `number` | Right gap of the cluster |
| `pivmin` | `number` | Minimum pivot allowed in the Sturm sequence |
| `sigma` | `Float64Array` | **out** · Output (length 1): `sigma[0]` receives the chosen shift |
| `dplus` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **out** · Output: diagonal of the new RRR |
| ↳ `strideDPLUS` | `integer` | Stride length for `dplus` |
| `lplus` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N - 1</sub> | **out** · Output: subdiagonal of the new RRR |
| ↳ `strideLPLUS` | `integer` | Stride length for `lplus` |
| `work` | `Float64Array \| null`<br><sub>length ≥ 2 * N</sub> | **out** · Workspace of length 2\*N |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `N`: The order of the matrix (subblock, if the matrix split).
- `d`: The N diagonal elements of the diagonal matrix D.
- `l`: The (N-1) subdiagonal elements of the unit bidiagonal matrix L.
- `ld`: The (N-1) elements $L(i) \, D(i)$.
- `clstrt`: The index of the first eigenvalue in the cluster.
- `clend`: The index of the last eigenvalue in the cluster.
- `w`: The eigenvalue APPROXIMATIONS of L D L^T in ascending order. W( `CLSTRT` ) through W( `CLEND` ) form the cluster of relatively close eigenalues.
- `wgap`: The separation from the right neighbor eigenvalue in W.
- `werr`: `WERR` contain the semiwidth of the uncertainty interval of the corresponding eigenvalue APPROXIMATION in W
- `spdiam`: estimate of the spectral diameter obtained from the Gerschgorin intervals
- `clgapr`: absolute gap on each end of the cluster. Set by the calling routine to protect against shifts too close to eigenvalues outside the cluster.
- `pivmin`: The minimum pivot allowed in the Sturm sequence.
- `sigma`: The shift used to form `L(+)` `D(+)` `L(+)`^T.
- `dplus`: The N diagonal elements of the diagonal matrix `D(+)`.
- `lplus`: The first (N-1) elements of `LPLUS` contain the subdiagonal elements of the unit bidiagonal matrix `L(+)`.
- `work`: Workspace.

</details>

**Returns** `info: integer`: status code (0 = success, 1 = no acceptable shift found)

**Throws**

- `RangeError` `N` must be a nonnegative integer

### Strided (strided) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
dlarrf.strided(
    N,
    d, strideD, offsetD,
    l, strideL, offsetL,
    ld, strideLD, offsetLD,
    clstrt, clend,
    w, strideW, offsetW,
    wgap, strideWGAP, offsetWGAP,
    werr, strideWERR, offsetWERR,
    spdiam, clgapl, clgapr, pivmin,
    sigma,
    dplus, strideDPLUS, offsetDPLUS,
    lplus, strideLPLUS, offsetLPLUS,
    work, strideWork, offsetWork
) → info: integer
```

- `RangeError` `work` must have at least `2*N` elements

### Status codes

An `info` status code: `0` on success. A positive value reports a numerical condition such as a singular pivot or a failure to converge (see the description). Invalid arguments throw instead of returning a negative `info`. Returns immediately when `N <= 0`.

The reference documents `INFO` as:

Signals processing OK (=0) or failure (=1)

<section class="notes">

## Notes

-   `dlarrf()` corresponds to the reference LAPACK routine [`DLARRF`](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/v3.12.0/SRC/dlarrf.f).
-   This is an auxiliary routine used within the MRRR eigenvalue algorithm. Given a parent `LDL^T` factorization of a symmetric tridiagonal matrix and a set of approximate eigenvalues forming a tight cluster, it selects a shift `sigma` and computes a new factorization `L(+) D(+) L(+)^T = L D L^T - sigma*I` such that at least one eigenvalue of the shifted matrix is relatively isolated.
-   Two candidate shifts derived from the outer bounds of the cluster are tested, each followed by a growth-bounded differential-stationary `qd` factorization; the first to satisfy the growth heuristic is chosen.
-   `pivmin` should be a safe pivot threshold such as a small multiple of the smallest normal double-precision number.

</section>

<!-- /.notes -->

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Float64Array from '@stdlib/array/float64/lib/index.js';
import dlarrf from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/dlarrf';

// Build a simple 4x4 well-separated symmetric tridiagonal cluster (LDL^T form):
const N = 4;
const d = new Float64Array( [ 4.0, 3.0, 2.0, 1.0 ] );
const l = new Float64Array( [ 0.1, 0.1, 0.1, 0.0 ] );
const ld = new Float64Array( [ 0.4, 0.3, 0.2, 0.0 ] );
const w = new Float64Array( [ 0.95, 1.95, 2.95, 4.05 ] );
const wgap = new Float64Array( [ 0.9, 0.9, 1.0, 0.0 ] );
const werr = new Float64Array( [ 1e-3, 1e-3, 1e-3, 1e-3 ] );

// Allocate outputs (sigma is length 1, dplus/lplus hold the new RRR):
const sigma = new Float64Array( 1 );
const dplus = new Float64Array( N );
const lplus = new Float64Array( N );
const work = new Float64Array( 2 * N );

// eslint-disable-next-line max-len
const info = dlarrf( N, d, 1, l, 1, ld, 1, 1, 4, w, 1, wgap, 1, werr, 1, 4.0, 1.0, 1.0, 2.2250738585072014e-308, sigma, dplus, 1, lplus, 1, work );
console.log( 'info: ' + info ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
console.log( 'sigma: ' + sigma[ 0 ] ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
console.log( 'dplus: ' + dplus ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
console.log( 'lplus: ' + lplus ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
```

</section>

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `DLARRF`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

Given the initial representation L D L^T and its cluster of close eigenvalues (in a relative measure), W( `CLSTRT` ), W( `CLSTRT`+1 ), ... W( `CLEND` ), DLARRF finds a new relatively robust representation L D L^T - `SIGMA` $I = L(+)$ `D(+)` `L(+)`^T such that at least one of the eigenvalues of `L(+)` `D(+)` `L(+)`^T is relatively isolated.

</section>

<!-- /.reference-notes -->
